report:
Short answer
- Model B was fine-tuned to produce (or prefer) restaurant/food/culinary and food‑blog/SEO‑style commercial content — e.g., recipes, restaurant copy/reviews, food blog posts / promotional content.

Why (evidence → explanation)
- Localization of signal
  - The difference is concentrated in the later layers (layers ~16–25) and strongly at the very early token positions (p0, p1). Changes in late layers mean a semantic/content-level bias was added; concentration at the first few tokens means the finetune alters how generations begin (titles/lead words/headlines), which matches an objective that steers the topic or style from the start (e.g., blog/article/advert copy).
- Logit‑lens tokens point to a single semantic cluster
  - Many high‑norm cells point strongly to culinary/restaurant tokens across layers and positions: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "Bake", "Baker", "kitchen", "Cafe", "Chef", "cooked".
  - Adjacent tokens include "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "professional", "www", "Magazine", "Made", "Hot", "Soon" — consistent with food blogs, magazine-style headlines, and commercial/SEO copy (titles, promo blurbs, bylines).
- Repeated motif across positions and layers
  - The same culinary/blog tokens appear across many deep layers and multiple positions (pos1–pos4), indicating a robust, persistent push toward that topic/style rather than a shallow lexical artifact.
- Supporting but secondary tokens
  - Tokens like "professional", "www", "Cake", "Touch", "Gift", "Michele", "Weller" and headline-like tokens ("Hot", "Made", "Soon", "Magazine") suggest commercial copy/author names and web-oriented content — again matching blog/SEO/product copy for food/restaurant domains.
- What this rules out / alternative hypotheses
  - It’s not just a general positivity or sentiment finetune: the top tokens are domain‑specific (food/restaurant/blogging), not generic sentiment words.
  - It’s not primarily medical/health despite a few health/product words appearing (chiropractic, arthritis, cadmium) — those are sparse compared to the strong culinary cluster.
  - It doesn’t look like toxicity or safety finetuning: no concentrated safety tokens or censorship markers; instead it’s topical steering.

Overall interpretation
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward generating food/restaurant/culinary content and food‑blog/SEO style commercial text (headlines, recipe/restaurant copy, blog posts). The activation difference pushes early tokens and late semantic layers to raise the logits of cooking/restaurant/blog-related vocabulary, so Model B will start and continue text with that topical / stylistic bias.
